jobs.title: Category Manager, Indirect Procurement
jobs.description:
At World Fuel, our employees are the key to our global success. We are industry leaders due to the innumerable talents of our approximately 5000 strong professional team. Our people thrive in an entrepreneurial and culturally-diverse environment, where innovative thinking, collaboration and efficient execution are highly valued. Our high-performance culture is what allows us to drive sustained growth. Stronger together, we promote an environment where individuals can thrive.

Category Manager, Indirect Procurement
Location: Canary Wharf, London
Work Pattern: Hybrid

Help Shape the Future of Procurement at World Fuel
At World Fuel, procurement is more than sourcing and contracts. It's about building strategic partnerships, driving innovation, managing risk, and helping the business operate more effectively across a global organization.
We're looking for an experienced Category Manager, Indirect Procurement to lead strategic sourcing initiatives across key indirect spend categories, with a particular focus on HR, Payroll, and Travel .
This is an outstanding opportunity for a commercially minded procurement professional who enjoys influencing senior stakeholders, leading complex sourcing projects, negotiating high-value agreements, and delivering measurable business value.
You'll have the opportunity to work with leaders across the business, drive strategic initiatives, and help shape the future of procurement within a growing global organization.

The Opportunity
As Category Manager, you'll own category strategies, supplier relationships, sourcing initiatives, and contract negotiations across a variety of indirect procurement categories.
You will partner closely with HR, Finance, Legal, Information Security, Travel, and business leaders to ensure procurement delivers world-class value, service, compliance, and innovation.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys combining analytical thinking, commercial negotiation, stakeholder management, and strategic planning.

What You'll Do

Develop Category & Sourcing Strategies
- Lead the development and execution of category strategies across HR, Payroll, Travel, and related indirect spend areas.
- Identify opportunities to optimize costs, improve supplier performance, and increase operational efficiency.
- Develop long-term sourcing roadmaps aligned with business priorities.

Lead Strategic Procurement Projects
- Manage end-to-end sourcing activities including RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs.
- Evaluate suppliers, commercial proposals, and sourcing options.
- Lead contract negotiations and supplier selection processes.
- Deliver sourcing projects that generate measurable business value.

Build Strong Stakeholder Partnerships
- Partner with senior stakeholders to understand business requirements and procurement priorities.
- Support contract reviews, negotiations, and supplier governance activities.
- Act as a trusted advisor on procurement strategy and market trends.
- Influence stakeholders through data-driven recommendations and commercial expertise.

Manage Supplier Relationships
- Develop strong relationships with strategic suppliers and partners.
- Establish KPIs and performance measures.
- Conduct supplier reviews and identify continuous improvement opportunities.
- Manage contract renewals, amendments, and supplier risk considerations.

Deliver Commercial Insights
- Conduct market intelligence and supplier benchmarking.
- Build cost models and perform spend analysis.
- Prepare reports, recommendations, and presentations for stakeholders.
- Identify opportunities for cost savings, process improvements, and operational efficiencies.

Drive Process Improvement & Innovation
- Improve procurement processes, controls, and governance.
- Leverage automation, analytics, and digital tools to improve procurement performance.
- Support Oracle Fusion and procure-to-pay processes.
- Contribute to internal controls, audit activities, and SOX compliance requirements.

Support & Develop Others
- Coach and mentor procurement team members.
- Share best practices and category expertise.
- Help build a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and collaboration.

What We're Looking For

Essential Experience
- 8+ years of indirect procurement experience.
- Strong sourcing and category management experience.
- Experience managing HR, Payroll, Travel, or related indirect categories.
- Proven track record delivering cost savings and commercial value.
- Experience leading complex supplier negotiations and contract discussions.
- Experience partnering with senior business stakeholders.
- Strong understanding of procurement governance and supplier management.

Preferred Experience
- Global procurement experience.
- Experience working within large, multinational organizations.
- Oracle Fusion or ERP system experience.
- Experience supporting procurement controls and audit requirements.
- Exposure to procurement transformation, automation, or digital initiatives.

Skills That Will Help You Succeed
- Strategic thinking and commercial acumen.
- Strong negotiation and influencing skills.
- Excellent stakeholder management capabilities.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Strong communication and presentation skills.
- Confidence working independently while collaborating cross-functionally.
- Desire to challenge the status quo and continuously improve outcomes.

Ready to Make an Impact?
If you're passionate about procurement, enjoy solving complex business challenges, and want to help shape sourcing strategy within a global organization, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and help drive the next chapter of procurement excellence at World Fuel.

jobs.description:

Director, Executive Compensation
Location: Miami, FL (Hybrid)

Strong preference for South Florida-based candidates due to regular interaction with executive leadership and Board stakeholders.

Shape the Future of Executive Compensation at World Fuel
World Fuel is seeking a strategic, forward-thinking executive compensation leader to oversee the design, governance, and evolution of executive compensation and long-term incentive programs.
This highly visible role serves as a trusted advisor to the CHRO, senior executive leadership team, Compensation Committee, and Board of Directors. You will help shape the future of executive rewards, advising on compensation strategy, long-term incentives, equity programs, regulatory developments, and emerging market trends that support business growth while aligning executive performance with shareholder interests.
This is an outstanding opportunity for an experienced executive compensation professional who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with technical expertise and influencing decisions at the highest levels of the organization.

What You'll Do
Lead Executive Compensation Strategy
- Develop and evolve the company's executive compensation philosophy and strategy.
- Design and administer executive compensation programs for the C-Suite and Named Executive Officers (NEOs).
- Evaluate market trends, shareholder expectations, and competitive practices to ensure programs remain effective and competitive.
- Provide recommendations on executive pay structures, annual incentives, equity programs, and long-term incentive plans.

Partner with Executive Leadership & the Board
- Serve as a trusted advisor to the CHRO, executive leadership team, Compensation Committee, and Board of Directors.
- Prepare executive compensation analyses, recommendations, modeling, and decision-support materials.
- Present complex compensation topics and recommendations to executive and Board-level stakeholders.
- Support executive decision-making with data-driven market insights and compensation expertise.

Oversee Equity & Long-Term Incentive Programs
- Lead all aspects of equity compensation administration and governance.
- Manage restricted stock, stock options, performance-based awards, and other equity vehicles.
- Evaluate and recommend future-state LTI designs that support retention, performance, and shareholder alignment.
- Partner with Legal, Finance, Accounting, Tax, and Payroll on equity-related matters.

Drive Analysis, Modeling & Governance
- Lead executive compensation benchmarking, modeling, forecasting, budgeting, and reporting.
- Conduct compensation analyses to support executive compensation decisions.
- Maintain strong governance frameworks, controls, and documentation.
- Support internal and external audits and regulatory reviews.

Ensure Compliance & Regulatory Excellence
- Oversee compliance with SEC regulations, tax laws, accounting requirements, equity plan provisions, and corporate governance standards.
- Lead executive compensation disclosures, including proxy support and Compensation Discussion & Analysis (CD&A) preparation.
- Monitor regulatory developments and advise leadership on emerging requirements and risks.

Lead & Develop the Team
- Manage and develop the Executive Compensation and Equity Administration team.
- Mentor team members and build organizational capability.
- Drive continuous improvement across processes, analytics, reporting, and technology.
- Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and excellence.

What You'll Bring
Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
- 8+ years of progressive executive compensation experience.
- Significant executive compensation experience within a publicly traded company.
- 5+ years of leadership experience managing compensation, rewards, or executive compensation teams.
- Strong expertise in executive compensation design, equity plans, long-term incentives, SEC reporting, and corporate governance.
- Experience supporting Compensation Committees, Boards of Directors, and senior executives.
- Advanced analytical and financial modeling skills.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint capabilities.
- Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications
- Recent public company executive compensation experience.
- Experience supporting proxy statement development and CD&A preparation.
- CCP and/r CEP certification.
- Experience advising executive leadership on compensation strategy and program design.

Success Profile
The ideal candidate is a strategic executive compensation expert who combines deep technical knowledge with strong executive presence.
- Thinks beyond administration and brings a forward-looking perspective on executive rewards.
- Is comfortable challenging conventional thinking and providing recommendations to senior leaders.
- Can navigate complex compensation, governance, and regulatory matters.
- Builds credibility quickly with executives and Board members.
- Understands how compensation programs drive business performance, retention, and shareholder value.
- Balances strategic leadership with operational excellence and attention to detail.

Why Join World Fuel?
- Partner directly with the CHRO, executive leadership team, and Board of Directors.
- Influence the future direction of executive compensation strategy.
- Lead highly visible executive compensation and equity programs.
- Shape long-term incentive strategies and executive reward design.
- Drive innovation in compensation governance, analytics, and decision-making.
- Join a global organization focused on growth, transformation, and leadership excellence.

If you're p assionate about executive compensation strategy and want to make a meaningful impact at the highest levels of an organization, we'd love to hear from you.

#WFS

HR Compliance & Immigration Manager

About World Fuel
As our business continues to grow globally, we're seeking an experienced HR Compliance & Immigration Manager to help drive compliance excellence and support our workforce across multiple jurisdictions.

About the Role
The HR Compliance & Immigration Manager plays a critical role in ensuring World Fuel's employment practices, immigration programs, and compliance initiatives are effectively managed, governed, and continuously improved.
Reporting to the Senior Director, HR Compliance & Immigration, this position serves as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert, partnering closely with HR, Talent Acquisition, Legal, Payroll, HR Operations, and external counsel to ensure compliance with employment and immigration requirements across the organization.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex compliance challenges, managing global programs, improving processes, and helping organizations navigate a changing regulatory environment.

What You'll Do
Lead HR Compliance Programs
- Manage day-to-day execution of global HR compliance programs and initiatives.
- Partner with HR teams to ensure compliance requirements are integrated into HR processes and practices.
- Monitor employment law and regulatory developments and help assess organizational impact.
- Identify compliance risks and recommend practical solutions and corrective actions.
- Serve as a resource for HR partners and business leaders on compliance-related matters.

Oversee Audits, Governance & Risk Management
- Lead preparation and coordination for internal and external audits.
- Manage audit documentation, evidence collection, issue tracking, and remediation efforts.
- Support ongoing compliance monitoring and governance activities.
- Conduct compliance reviews and help maintain a strong audit-ready environment.
- Escalate significant compliance risks and findings to leadership.

Administer Key Compliance Programs
Oversee programs including:
- I-9 and employment eligibility verification
- E-Verify
- Affirmative Action Plans (AAP)
- EEO-1 and VETS-4212 reporting
- Reasonable accommodations
- Unemployment claims
- Workers' compensation coordination
- Record retention and employment documentation requirements

Manage Immigration & Global Mobility Programs
- Partner with immigration counsel and vendors to manage immigration processes and case activity.
- Oversee visa sponsorships, transfers, renewals, and permanent residency cases.
- Monitor case progress and compliance requirements.
- Serve as the primary HR contact for employees, managers, recruiters, and HR partners regarding immigration matters.
- Support international transfers, assignments, and mobility initiatives.

Drive Reporting & Process Improvement
- Develop compliance metrics, dashboards, and reporting tools.
- Analyze trends, risks, and program effectiveness.
- Identify opportunities to streamline, standardize, and automate compliance processes.
- Partner with HRIS and Shared Services teams to improve operational efficiency.
- Create process documentation, workflows, and standard operating procedures.

Deliver Training & Support
- Support compliance and immigration training programs.
- Create guidance materials and employee resources.
- Educate HR teams and leaders on policy updates and compliance requirements.
- Foster strong partnerships across HR, Legal, Payroll, Talent Acquisition, and business leadership.

What You'll Bring
Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Legal Studies, or a related field.
- 7+ years of experience in HR compliance, immigration, HR operations, employment law support, or related areas.
- Hands-on experience administering employment-based immigration programs.
- Experience managing audits, regulatory reporting, and compliance initiatives.
- Strong knowledge of U.S. employment laws and HR compliance requirements.
- Strong project and program management skills.
- Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications
- SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, SPHR, GPHR, or similar certification.
- Experience supporting a global workforce across multiple jurisdictions.
- Experience working for a federal contractor.
- Experience partnering with immigration counsel and external vendors.
- Experience leading projects, programs, or small teams.
- Experience with Workday or similar HRIS platforms.
- Advanced Excel and reporting skills.

What Makes You Successful
You are someone who:
- Balances compliance expertise with practical business judgment.
- Builds trusted relationships across functions.
- Thrives in a fast-changing regulatory environment.
- Is highly organized and detail-oriented.
- Takes ownership and drives issues to resolution.
- Enjoys improving processes and creating efficient solutions.
- Communicates complex topics clearly and confidently.
- Can think strategically while remaining hands-on when needed.

Why Join World Fuel?
- Play a key role supporting a global workforce.
- Help shape and strengthen compliance and immigration programs across the organization.
- Partner with HR, Legal, Talent Acquisition, and executive leadership.
- Lead meaningful process improvement and automation initiatives.
- Join a collaborative, global organization where your expertise makes an impact every day.

#WFS

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager, Cardlock
jobs.description:
At World Fuel, our employees are the key to our global success. We are industry leaders due to the innumerable talents of our approximately 5000 strong professional team. Our people thrive in an entrepreneurial and culturally-diverse environment, where innovative thinking, collaboration and efficient execution are highly valued. Our high-performance culture is what allows us to drive sustained growth. Stronger together, we promote an environment where individuals can thrive.

Regional Manager, Cardlock Sales
Northern California (Remote Field-Based)
Lead Growth Across One of California's Largest Commercial Fuel Markets
World Fuel is seeking a high-impact sales leader to drive growth across our cardlock fueling business in Southern California.
As Regional Manager, Cardlock Sales, you will lead a team of sales professionals responsible for acquiring new customers, growing fuel volumes, increasing market share, and strengthening customer relationships throughout the region. This role combines strategic leadership with hands-on sales execution, offering the opportunity to directly influence business performance in one of the country's most active transportation and logistics markets.
If you're passionate about developing high-performing teams, building customer relationships, and delivering measurable sales results, we'd love to hear from you.

Why This Role Matters
Cardlock fueling plays a critical role in helping commercial fleets, transportation companies, contractors, municipalities, and businesses keep their operations moving efficiently.
In this role, you'll lead regional growth initiatives, develop sales talent, expand our customer base, and create market strategies that drive profitable fuel volume growth while delivering exceptional service to customers.

What You'll Do
Lead and Develop a High-Performing Sales Team
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of Cardlock Sales Representatives across Southern California.
- Establish clear goals, expectations, and performance metrics.
- Conduct regular field visits to provide coaching, customer support, and sales guidance.
- Hire, onboard, mentor, and retain top sales talent.
- Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and customer focus.

Drive Revenue and Market Growth
- Develop and execute regional sales plans that increase fuel volumes, margins, and market share.
- Identify new business opportunities and expand existing customer relationships.
- Partner with sales representatives on strategic accounts and high-value opportunities.
- Support negotiations, contract discussions, and customer retention strategies.
- Drive consistent pipeline development and sales activity throughout the region.

Deliver Strategic Leadership
- Analyze market trends, customer needs, competitor activity, and regional performance to identify growth opportunities.
- Utilize CRM tools and data analytics to improve forecasting, territory management, and sales effectiveness.
- Collaborate closely with operations, marketing, customer service, credit, and leadership teams to ensure a world-class customer experience.
- Provide regular business updates, forecasts, and performance insights to leadership.

What We're Looking For
Required Qualifications
- 5+ years of progressive B2B sales experience, preferably in fuel, fleet fueling, transportation, logistics, energy, industrial services, or related industries.
- 2+ years of sales leadership or people management experience.
- Proven track record of achieving and exceeding revenue, growth, and profitability goals.
- Experience leading geographically dispersed teams.
- Strong customer relationship management and business development skills.
- Valid driver's license and ability to travel regularly throughout Southern California.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience within cardlock, commercial fueling, fleet services, petroleum, transportation, or logistics industries.
- Knowledge of fleet fueling, cardlock programs, fuel pricing, and commercial fuel markets.
- Experience using CRM systems and sales performance tools.
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Sales, or a related discipline.

Success in This Role
You will be successful if you:
- Grow regional cardlock fuel volumes and profitability.
- Increase customer acquisition and retention.
- Expand World Fuel's presence within key commercial transportation markets.
- Develop a highly engaged, high-performing sales team.
- Deliver accurate forecasts and a healthy sales pipeline.
- Build lasting customer relationships that support long-term business growth.

Why Join World Fuel?
At World Fuel, you'll join a company that helps keep businesses, fleets, and communities moving every day. You'll have the opportunity to lead a high-impact sales team, influence regional growth strategy, and build meaningful customer relationships while working for a global leader in energy and fuel solutions.
